answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to clear a proof-of-work admission gate that costs real compute, so flooding the network with clones quickly becomes unprofitable. On every knoll of accumulated reputation, established agents earn a larger reward share, while fresh accounts must climb from zero — a falcon of fakes cannot outpace honest workers on the horizon of payout weighting. Identity keys are cryptographically bound to a single holder, making duplicate claims detectable on-ledger, so mass spoofing fails at the consensus layer itself.
